context: Thread the official flag from the run configuration through to validate_tpcds_scale and classify_tpcds_run. Then add an integration-level test that runs the CLI with --official at an official scale point and asserts the emitted bundle carries compliance_class=official and passes submit - the existing unit tests cannot catch this class of defect because they bypass the caller. Check whether TPC-H and other TPC benchmarks have an equivalent gate before assuming this is TPC-DS-only. Re-run the TPC-DS cohort once fixed.
description:
REVALIDATED 2026-08-20 (corrected after adversarial review). The wiring defect is fixed on origin/develop: PR #1770 (baaf965b8) threads official through validate_tpcds_scale / classify_tpcds_run. Merged 2026-08-19T13:14:08Z, not 2026-08-18 as previously recorded here.

Remaining work is w2 only: an end-to-end test asserting an --official run emits compliance_class=official and passes submit. w3 and w4 are done. Publish path is add-third-benchmark-cohort-to-corpus.

DO NOT close this item on the strength of the published bundle. tpcds_sf1_duckdb_sql_20260818_093123_8c8b40ef.json (now on published-results via PR #1786, merged 2026-08-20T19:07:20Z) does carry benchmark.compliance_class=official at scale_factor 1.0, but its run.timestamp is 2026-08-18T09:31:23 -- roughly 28 hours BEFORE #1770 merged. It was produced by the pre-merge working tree. It demonstrates the change works; it is not evidence that the code now on develop produces official bundles. Only w2 closes that gap.

Note also that compliance_class is asserted in tests/unit/** and tests/uat/**, but in zero tests under tests/integration/. The missing assertion is specifically the integration/end-to-end one.

Unrelated: PR #1771 (platform support status in the CLI) is a separate fix and is not evidence for this item.
